description: Classical Mechanics begins with the Lagrangian formulation and assumes first-year Newtonian mechanics (Newton's laws in inertial frames, energy, momentum and angular momentum). The source course, MIT 8.09, assumes two earlier mechanics courses; Corniversity reviews the Newtonian material inside unit 1 and offers the bridge course for anyone who wants it first.

Special Relativity contrasts Lorentz with Galilean kinematics and relativistic with Newtonian momentum and energy, so first-year Newtonian mechanics is assumed (MIT 8.20 lists 8.01 Classical Mechanics as a prerequisite). The mathematics needed is linear algebra and single-variable calculus.

General Relativity I starts from Minkowski spacetime written in index notation, four-vectors and the Lorentz group; without special relativity the first unit cannot be followed. This is the only hard rule in the physics department.

The MIT 8.962 syllabus asks for familiarity with Lagrangians and action principles, differential equations and linear algebra; the variational derivation of the field equation and the geodesic action use them.
